- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Victorian-era vases were produced from 1837-1901 and were a staple of home decor.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common materials used for Victorian-era vases include ceramic (earthenware, stoneware, porcelain), glass, metal (bronze, copper, silver), and porcelain-bisque.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable manufacturers of Victorian-era vases include Wedgwood, Royal Worcester, and Minton.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common styles of Victorian-era vases include Orientalism, Rococo Revival, Neo-Classicism, Aesthetic Movement, and Art Nouveau.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Decoration techniques for Victorian-era vases included transfer printing, hand-painting, gilding, and enamelwork.

- [USER] The user is particularly interested in learning about the Aesthetic Movement style and its common motifs and designs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Aesthetic Movement (c. 1860-1900) emphasized beauty, taste, and sensuality, reacting against strict Victorian values.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common motifs in the Aesthetic Movement include florals (peonies, lilies, sunflowers), birds (peacocks, parrots, swallows), foliage, insects (butterflies, bees), geometric patterns, Asian influences, and luxurious materials.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Identifying Aesthetic Movement designs involves looking for ornate decoration, floral motifs, birds and insects, geometric patterns, Asian influences, luxurious materials, and whiplash curves.
- [USER] The user is curious about the Art Nouveau style and how it differs from the Aesthetic Movement.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Art Nouveau (c. 1890-1910) is characterized by organic forms, sinuous lines, whiplash motifs, and nature inspiration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key differences between Art Nouveau and the Aesthetic Movement include Art Nouveau's more radical and experimental nature, greater emphasis on line and form, less focus on decoration, and more international influence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Identifying Art Nouveau designs involves looking for organic forms and lines, whiplash motifs, nature inspiration, and innovative materials and techniques.
